one_line_contribution: A crossover design in ALFWorld (the 'task-type provenance square') that labels both a procedural memory bank and a GEPA-optimized instruction by which task types' episodes produced them, and reports with a confidence interval the fraction of the bank's task-type-specific advantage that has already been absorbed by an instruction written from those same episodes.
closest_prior_work: ExpeL (arXiv 2308.10144) is the work that most threatens novelty, and the proposal cites it five times without ever confronting the part that bites. ExpeL's learned artifact is a natural-language insights block distilled from training episodes and prepended to the prompt, and its published ablations already separate that block from the retrieved-trajectory demonstrations drawn from the same training pool, evaluated in ALFWorld among other environments. That is a version of 'what fraction of a retrieved-experience system's gain is already held by the instruction-shaped container built from the same episodes,' in this exact environment, already in print. The proposal concedes 'memory as an instruction is not a framing we invented' but then claims 'nobody has reported the number' -- a claim ExpeL's own ablation table substantially undercuts. What genuinely survives is narrower than the proposal presents: ExpeL fills both containers from one undifferentiated pool, so it never manipulates episode provenance and never runs the crossover, and its insights are not written by a reflective prompt optimizer. AutoManual (arXiv 2405.16247, NeurIPS 2024) independently pre-empts the compiled-block arm in ALFWorld (conceded in v5.2), and MIPROv2 (arXiv 2406.11695) pre-empts the two-container ablation on a single training set. Stacked together, the residual contribution is the interaction estimand and the CI on it.
strongest_objection: The confirmatory endpoint does not measure the quantity the title and abstract claim, and the pre-registration contradicts itself about what licenses the claim. (1) Inner(I) = acc(I x B_own) - acc(I x B_oth) is the bank's task-type DISCRIMINABILITY, not its value. A >= 0.5 says the on-type-versus-off-type bank contrast roughly halves when the instruction is on-type; that is entirely compatible with the bank still adding, say, +6pt over no-memory at I_own. 'Is your agent's memory just an un-optimized prompt' requires g(I_own, B_own) to go to zero, and that quantity is never confirmatory: it appears only as row 5's g(I_all, B_all) under a +/-3pt TOST that the proposal itself computes is declarable only when the observed effect is within ~0.2pt of zero. The headline is therefore ridden on an endpoint that cannot establish it while the endpoint that could is pre-declared nearly unpassable. (2) The document double-specifies its own decision rule. Experiments states, in bold, 'Both must pass; nothing else gates the confirmatory claim' for A and A0, while Rule M states 'absorption is claimed only if the help term carries >= 2/3 of DeltaInner,' and Prediction 7 restates Rule M as a required outcome. In the live case where A and A0 both clear threshold but the off term carries the shrinkage, the pre-registration says both that absorption is claimed and that the reading is distractor-robustness. A design whose entire pitch is that every decision rule is fixed in advance cannot leave its headline decision ambiguous. (3) The co-primary structure buys less than advertised. A is inflated by the mis-specification/repair channel the proposal admits; A0's denominator Inner(I0*) is measured at the short hand-written scaffold, so A0 is inflated by the generic context-competition mechanism the proposal itself cites (arXiv 2604.27003) -- a long, directive optimized instruction competes with ANY injected block regardless of provenance. An intersection-union test controls type-I error only if each marginal null is unbiased; here both marginals are biased toward passing, by different mechanisms, so requiring both to pass is not the protection it is presented as. (4) Self-conceded and decisive for the title: risk 26 admits the instruction-side episode-versus-type test (A_epi) is under-powered at SE ~= 0.30 and de-thresholded, and that its Tier-0 replacement (row 17, B'_own) answers a different question. So 'the same training episodes in two containers' -- the title's actual claim -- is not tested at power by any Tier-0 arm on the container the paper is named for.
what_would_fix_it: 1) Make the practitioner quantity confirmatory: pre-register the retention ratio R = g(I_own, B_own) / g(I0* , B_own) -- every term already exists at n = 1,200 in rows 1, 2 and 3, so it costs nothing -- and title the paper after whichever endpoint the design can actually establish rather than after one it cannot. 2) Promote I_type to Tier 0 (~25,500 calls, ~2 hours, ~2.5% of Tier 0). 3) Resolve the Rule M versus 'single operational bar' contradiction with an explicit truth table over the {A, A0, Rule M, Rule R} outcome space, so no post-hoc reading is available. 4) Use the resources the track actually offers: the brief specifies 4xA100 and a frontier API for the reflector role at a few hundred dollars, and the proposal restricts itself to two GPUs and asserts 'there is no API key on this node,' then justifies cutting the third optimizer seed, the coupling arm (row 13), the step control (row 15) and I_type by an 84-hour ceiling that is an artifact of using half the available hardware -- while G2 (optimizer must beat I0* by 3pt) is at risk mainly because the reflector is a local 32B. Restoring the stated resources removes most of the refusals and most of the G2 risk at once. 5) Run the freeze-blocking provenance-crossover search and report its results in the submission, not merely promise it before DESIGN.md, and add a numerical confrontation with ExpeL's insights-versus-retrieval ablation to Related Work. 6) Report the ALFWorld throughput measurement before claiming the compute plan, since the entire 60-84h figure is transferred from a 6-call-per-episode QA setting with far shorter prompts.
missing_baseline: I_type -- the hand-written instruction given only the three task-type names and their canonical skeleton, with no episodes at all. This is the rival explanation for the entire headline result: an optimized instruction that absorbed nothing episode-specific, and merely encodes which task family the held-out games belong to, would produce exactly the predicted shrinkage in Inner(I_own) versus Inner(I_oth). The proposal has already designed and hashed it, prices it at ~25,500 calls, and then demotes it to Tier 1 on the reasoning that 'its decisive role was interpreting a branch that is no longer a decision rule' -- while a 500-game graded planted control (row 9), an 800-game compile-once arm (row 11) whose novelty is explicitly disclaimed, and an 800-game joint-optimization arm stay at Tier 0. That ordering is indefensible: I_type is the cheapest arm in the design that can kill the paper's own interpretation. A reviewer will also demand the raw-context / long-context dump (R_raw, M_all) at Tier 0 rather than Tier 1, given that the proposal itself cites EvoMemBench and AutoMEM for the finding that naive long-context and flat-file baselines match engineered memory systems -- if a raw dump of the same episodes reproduces Inner, the distillation-and-retrieval container being 'absorbed' was never doing the work attributed to it.
preprint_collision: The check is the most conscientious part of the submission in form -- dated scans, query counts, per-ID verification channels, a corrected PDF read of ReasoningBank's Qwen gain (+3.6, not +7), and unusually frank concessions that EvoAgentBench publishes the qualitative headline and that ExpeL already stores memory as a prepended instruction. Judged as evidence for novelty, however, it is thin exactly where it is load-bearing. All four pre-freeze obligations are reported as UNRUN, including the freeze-blocking one: the search for held-out-episode and data-provenance crossovers in the prompt-optimization, contamination and data-attribution literatures. That is the search that decides whether the identification primitive -- the sole surviving novelty claim after the concessions -- is new, and the proposal states plainly that its novelty claim is conditional on a search that has not happened. That is a weakness, not a neutral. The check's demonstrated recall is also poor by its own account: it was weighted to the last six months and missed two directly on-point ALFWorld precedents from 2024 (AutoManual 2405.16247, AutoGuide 2403.08978) that a reviewer had to supply, and the pre-2026 window has still not been re-swept. Because arXiv is unreachable from the node, every 2026-dated competitor except EvoAgentBench rests on a single web-search channel, and every 'confirmed absent from the paper' claim except that one is asserted from abstracts -- which is precisely the kind of claim that cannot be established from an abstract. From my own knowledge, the pre-2026 IDs cited (2308.10144 ExpeL, 2406.11695 MIPROv2, 2405.16247 AutoManual, 2403.08978 AutoGuide, 2507.19457 GEPA, 2509.25140 ReasoningBank, 2502.12110 A-MEM, 2508.06433 Memp) are real and characterized accurately, which is a point in the check's favour; I cannot verify any of the 26xx identifiers, and every 'nobody has done this' assertion depends on them. I know of no preprint that runs this exact provenance crossover between an optimized instruction and a memory bank. But ExpeL's own ablation already reports a version of the two-container split on the same training episodes in ALFWorld, the compiled-block arm is conceded as a replication of AutoManual, and the crossover primitive is conceded as not the proposal's own -- so the collision that matters is not a single unfound preprint but the cumulative one the check itself documents.
